title: Daily Market Digest: Mixed Finish to Turbulent Week as Yields Hit 5%
subtitle: Friday, September 18, 2026 Market Close (Markets closed Saturday, September 19, 2026)

sections.title: Market Pulse: Yields Drive Mixed Close After Fed Hike

items.headline: U.S. equities closed a turbulent week with a mixed performance on Friday, September 18, 2026, as bond yields climbed to multi-year highs and investors continued to digest the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike.
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.00%, a level not seen since 2023, influencing market sentiment. Technology and semiconductor stocks demonstrated strength, while smaller companies and rate-sensitive sectors lagged. The week was marked by the Fed's first rate increase in three years, with indications of further tightening to combat persistent inflation.

items.headline: Schrodinger Leads Gainers
items.summary: Biotech firm Schrodinger ($SDGR) saw a significant surge, returning +26.4% on Friday.

items.headline: Coinbase Rises on SEC Exemption
items.summary: Coinbase Global ($COIN), a major cryptocurrency exchange, jumped +11.39% after the SEC issued a five-year conditional 'Innovation Exemption' for trading tokenized U.S. stocks, providing regulatory clarity for digital asset expansion.

items.headline: Robinhood Boosted by Tokenized Stock News
items.summary: Robinhood Markets ($HOOD) surged +7.93%, also benefiting from the SEC's 'Innovation Exemption' for tokenized securities, positioning the company to expand its offerings in this space.

items.headline: Xenon Pharma Tumbles on Trial Pause
items.summary: Xenon Pharmaceuticals ($XENE) tumbled -29.0% after temporarily pausing enrollment in trials for its experimental drug due to reported side effects.

items.headline: Fluence Energy Drops
items.summary: Fluence Energy ($FLNC) experienced a significant decline, falling -15.4% during Friday's trading session.

items.headline: Nucor Falls on Earnings Forecast
items.summary: Steelmaker Nucor ($NUE) declined -6.3% after forecasting its third-quarter earnings per share below analysts' mean estimates.

items.headline: Technology and Healthcare Lead, Utilities Lag This Week
items.summary: For the week ending September 18, 2026, healthcare was the best-performing sector, up 1.56%, followed by technology, which gained 1.03-1.1%. In contrast, utilities were the worst-performing sector, declining 2.95%, alongside financial services, which fell 2.29-2.35%.

items.headline: Fed Raises Rates, Signals Further Hikes Amid Inflation Concerns
items.summary: The Federal Reserve increased its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points earlier this week to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%, the first such move since July 2023. The central bank indicated that another rate hike is likely by year-end, with the median policy rate projected at 4.1% by the end of 2026, to combat persistent inflation.

items.headline: AI Boom Continues to Drive Durable Goods Orders
items.summary: The demand for AI infrastructure continues to be a significant economic driver, with durable goods orders expected to rise, primarily in computer and electrical equipment. This trend highlights ongoing investment in artificial intelligence technologies.

items.headline: US Initial Jobless Claims Fall, Mortgage Rates Climb
items.summary: Economic data released Friday showed U.S. initial jobless claims decreased to 196,000 for the week ending September 12, indicating a relatively healthy labor market. Concurrently, US mortgage rates reached their highest level since early 2025, reflecting the rising interest rate environment.

items.headline: Warren Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Hathaway Chairman
items.summary: Investing legend Warren Buffett announced he is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway ($BRK.A, $BRK.B) at 96, transitioning to chairman emeritus. His son, Howard Buffett, will take over as chairman, while Greg Abel remains CEO.

items.headline: Oil Prices Fluctuate Amid Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude prices remained volatile, briefly dipping below $102 a barrel before recovering above $103, as markets reacted to supply concerns following recent developments in geopolitical conflicts.
